packet.claim: recover_json_object ignores fenced objects when more than one code fence is present, contrary to the documented rule that the object scored is the last one inside a code fence when any fence holds one.
packet.execution_evidence: kernel recovery returned {"c":3} for the reproducer
packet.scope: inputs with more than one code fence containing JSON objects and at least one top-level object after the last fence
packet.source_basis: The object scored is the last one inside a code fence when any fence holds one, else the last top-level object in the text
packet.uncertainty: The phrase 'any fence holds one' could be read as 'at least one fence' or 'exactly one fence'; the code only handles exactly one fence, but the documented wording suggests at least one.
